sections.heading: Who We Are
sections.body:
The International Human Rights Council – USA (IHRC-USA) is an organization focused on human rights awareness, Research,Dignity, humanitarian values, peace, equality and community development.

IHRC-USA seeks to bring together individuals, volunteers, professionals, community leaders and organizations who share a commitment to human dignity and social responsibility.

Our approach emphasizes education, awareness, community participation, humanitarian service and constructive cooperation.

chairman-message.title: Chairman’s Message
chairman-message.subtitle: A message from the Chairman of IHRC-USA.

sections.heading: Dear Members, Volunteers, Partners, and Human Rights Defenders,
sections.body:
It is my great honor to present the International Human Rights Council – USA (IHRC-USA).

Human rights are the foundation of a peaceful, fair, and sustainable world. Every individual, regardless of nationality, race, gender, religion, social status, or background, deserves respect, dignity, equality, and justice.

IHRC-USA is committed to promoting and protecting fundamental human rights through awareness, education, humanitarian service, community empowerment, and international cooperation.

Our mission is guided by the principles of universal justice, compassion, integrity, accountability, and respect for human dignity.

Through the dedication of our members and partners around the world, we continue working toward a society where every person has the opportunity to live with freedom, safety, equality, and hope.

This handbook serves as a guiding document for our organization, explaining our vision, mission, values, responsibilities, and commitment to human rights principles.

I invite everyone to join hands with IHRC-USA in building a world based on peace, justice, equality, and humanity.

Together, we can create meaningful change.

sections.heading: With respect and commitment,
sections.body:
Chairman
International Human Rights Council – USA (IHRC-USA)
“Equal Justice for Everyone & Everywhere”

vision-mission.title: Vision & Mission
vision-mission.subtitle: What we aspire to and how we work towards it.

sections.heading: Our Vision
sections.body:
“A world where every person enjoys dignity, equality, freedom, justice and peace.”

Our vision is an inclusive society in which everyone is responsible for promoting and protecting human rights; everyone is respected and treated with equal dignity and respect; and the human rights of all are a reality, and a world in which human rights are universally recognized, respected, and protected.

We envision a society in which justice is upheld and every individual is empowered to live a life of dignity, freedom, and equality. We conduct research and take action to prevent and end human rights abuses, and to promote the values enshrined in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights and other internationally agreed human rights standards.

sections.heading: Our Mission
sections.body:
“To promote human-rights awareness, humanitarian values, peace, equality and community empowerment through education, advocacy, service, partnerships and responsible action.”

Our mission is to promote and protect the fundamental rights and freedoms of all individuals, regardless of race, gender, color, religion, language, or socio-economic status. We strive to create a society in which the rights of every person are upheld, respected, and protected without prejudice or discrimination.

Addressing the root causes of inequality, discrimination and injustice by changing laws, policies, practices and cultures. We do this through education, research, advocacy, investigation and monitoring.

We act as a driver for social change based on substantive equality principles. We fulfill our mission by exposing, challenging, and ending entrenched and pervasive structures and systems of discrimination through education, policy development, public inquiries, and litigation.

privacy-policy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy-policy.subtitle: How IHRC-USA collects, uses and protects your information.

sections.heading: Information We Collect
sections.body: We collect information you give us when you apply for membership, volunteer, contact us, verify a member or make a financial contribution. This may include your name, email address, phone number, address and any details you choose to share.

sections.heading: How We Use Your Information
sections.body: Your information is used to process membership applications, respond to enquiries, organise programs and events, send updates you have asked for, and meet our legal and reporting obligations.

sections.heading: Sharing of Information
sections.body: We do not sell or rent your personal information. We share it only with trusted service providers who help us run the website and our programs, or where disclosure is required by law.

sections.heading: Cookies
sections.body: This website may use essential cookies to work properly. We do not use cookies to track you across other websites.

sections.heading: Data Security
sections.body: We take reasonable steps to protect your information from loss, misuse and unauthorised access. No method of transmission over the internet is completely secure.

sections.heading: Your Rights
sections.body: You may ask to access, correct or delete the personal information we hold about you, or withdraw your consent to receive communications, at any time.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about this policy can be sent via the Contact page.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.subtitle: The terms that apply when you use this website.

sections.heading: Acceptance
sections.body: By accessing or using this website you agree to these Terms of Use. If you do not agree, please do not use the website.

sections.heading: Use of Content
sections.body: Content on this website is provided for information about our work and programs. You may not copy, modify or distribute it for commercial purposes without written permission.

sections.heading: Membership and Verification
sections.body: Membership applications are subject to review and approval. Member IDs and certificates remain the property of the organisation and must not be misused or transferred.

sections.heading: Financial contributions
sections.body: Financial contributions are voluntary and support our programs. Refunds are handled as described in our Refund Policy.

sections.heading: User Conduct
sections.body: You agree not to misuse the website, submit false information, or attempt to disrupt its operation or security.

sections.heading: Limitation of Liability
sections.body: We make every effort to keep information accurate but provide the website as is, without warranties of any kind.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: We may update these terms at any time. Continued use of the website means you accept the updated terms.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about these terms can be sent via the Contact page.

refund.title: Refund Policy
refund.subtitle: How refunds work for financial contributions and membership fees.

sections.heading: Financial contributions
sections.body: Financial contributions are voluntary contributions that fund our work and are generally non-refundable. If you made a financial contribution by mistake or were charged an incorrect amount, contact us within 14 days and we will review your request.

sections.heading: Membership Fees
sections.body: Membership fees are non-refundable once a membership has been approved and a Member ID issued. If your application is declined, any fee paid will be refunded in full.

sections.heading: Events and Programs
sections.body: If we cancel an event or program for which you paid a fee, you will receive a full refund or the option to transfer to a future date.

sections.heading: How to Request a Refund
sections.body: Send your request through the Contact page with your name, the date and amount of the payment, and the reason for the request. Please allow up to 14 working days for us to respond.

sections.heading: Processing Time
sections.body: Approved refunds are returned to the original payment method. Your bank or payment provider may take additional days to show the refund.

sections.heading: Contact
sections.body: Questions about this policy can be sent via the Contact page.

sections.heading: General Information
sections.body: The information on this website is provided by the IHRC-USA for general information and human rights awareness only. It is not legal advice and is not a substitute for advice from a qualified legal professional.

sections.heading: Accuracy
sections.body: We make reasonable efforts to keep the content accurate and up to date, but we do not guarantee that all information is complete or current. Content may be changed or removed without notice.

sections.heading: External Links
sections.body: This website may link to external websites. IHRC-USA is not responsible for the content or practices of those websites.

sections.heading: Use of Name and Logo
sections.body: The IHRC name and logo may not be used without written permission. Membership, positions and authority within IHRC can be confirmed only through official IHRC channels.

content.value: The International Human Rights Council–USA (IHRC-USA) is an independent, civil society organization (CSO). It is registered on the United Nations Partner Portal, and its organizational profile is featured on the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) website in connection with the Universal Periodic Review (UPR). Furthermore, IHRC-USA has completed the procedures for registration with the United Nations NGO Branch and is also registered on the European Commission’s EU Funding & Tenders Portal.

value.alt: UN Partner Portal – joint platform of UN agencies
UN Human Rights – Office of the High Commissioner

value.d: IHRC-USA is registered on the United Nations Partner Portal. The Portal is a platform for Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) to engage with the UN on partnership opportunities. It was developed jointly by IOM, the UN Secretariat, UN Women, FAO, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF, UNOPS, WFP and WHO to make collaboration between the UN and its partners harmonized, efficient and easy.

value.name: Integrity
value.text: The International Human Rights Council – USA is an independent civil society organization that pursues pressing issues. Its staff is highly committed to their work; Furthermore, they are not intimidated by governments or authorities from regions or geographical areas that do not comply with basic human rights standards. Grants for IHRC-USA are not accepted from donors who wish to direct operations or do not support our objectives.

value.name: Conduct
value.text: Must be honest and transparent. Use your powers responsibly. Report any misconduct. Avoid real or perceived conflicts of interest. Work to gain and maintain the trust of high-level public figures.

value.name: Neutrality
value.text: Make decisions and provide advice based on merit. Act without personal bias, greed, prejudice, or selfishness. Act objectively and fairly, considering all relevant facts and fair criteria. Implement government policies and programs equitably.

value.name: Accountability
value.text: Strive to set clear goals in a transparent manner. Accept your decisions and take responsibility for your actions. Endeavor to use resources in the best possible way. Subject yourself to appropriate self-examination.

value.name: Respect
value.text: Treat colleagues, other government officials, and the community fairly and objectively. Ensure freedom from discrimination, harassment, and bullying. Use this to continuously improve upon decisions. Share your opinions.

value.name: Leadership(P5)
value.text: Act vigorously to implement, encourage, and support these values. One must act independently and without bias, without identifying themselves with any political party or ideology. There should be no discrimination based on race, religion, language, caste, or gender when making decisions.

value.name: Support
value.text: Make decisions and provide advice in accordance with human rights. Act vigorously to implement, encourage, and support human rights. Promote human rights education.

value.name: Skills
value.text: Human rights defenders possess significant expertise in our fields. Our analysis is based on robust research and international human rights standards. IHRC-USA always strives for high-quality work, and staff seek to support the growth of the skills and expertise of local partners.

value.name: Performance
value.text: The International Human Rights Council – USA is a results-oriented and lean organization with strict financial controls and management. To ensure transparency, accountability, and learning in planning, monitoring, and evaluation, we use a results-based management system. We are able to adapt quickly to changing and volatile situations and have a high degree of flexibility when needed.

intro: IHRC-USA provides this complaint submission form as a channel for individuals who wish to report concerns, alleged misconduct, unfair treatment, harassment, discrimination, abuse, exploitation, or other matters affecting their rights, dignity, safety, or well-being.

This form is intended for individuals who have experienced harm or believe they have been affected by the actions, conduct, decisions, or omissions of another person, organization, institution, company, or other entity.
Every complaint should be treated respectfully, confidentially, impartially, and with appropriate care.
notice: Submitting a complaint does not automatically establish that an allegation is true.
IHRC-USA may review submissions within its organizational mandate and available capacity.
Submission of this form does not constitute a police report, court filing, or formal legal proceeding.
IHRC-USA does not replace police, courts, government authorities, emergency services, or qualified legal professionals.
If someone is in immediate danger, contact the appropriate local emergency services or law-enforcement authority without waiting for a response to this form.
who: Individuals who have personally experienced alleged misconduct or unfair treatment.
Individuals affected by the actions of another person.
Employees or former employees reporting workplace-related concerns.
Students or parents reporting concerns involving educational institutions.
Individuals reporting alleged discrimination, harassment, or exploitation.
Individuals affected by the conduct of an organization or institution.
Family members or authorized representatives submitting a complaint on behalf of an affected person, where appropriate.
Witnesses reporting concerns with the affected person's knowledge or where permitted by applicable procedures.
types: Community-related disputes involving rights or dignity.
Other matters involving human dignity, equality, safety, or welfare.
value.outside: Complaints outside the organization's mandate may be referred to an appropriate authority where lawful and suitable.
declaration: I confirm that the information provided in this complaint is accurate to the best of my knowledge.
I understand that submitting a complaint does not automatically establish that the allegations are proven.
I understand that IHRC-USA may review the information within its organizational mandate and available capacity.
I understand that IHRC-USA is not a court, police authority, or government enforcement agency.
I understand that further information may be requested where appropriate.

I understand that confidentiality will be handled in accordance with applicable privacy requirements and organizational policies, but absolute confidentiality cannot be guaranteed in every circumstance.
I confirm that I am authorized to provide the information submitted, where I am acting on behalf of another person.

value:
Human rights are the basic rights and freedoms that belong to every person simply because they are human. They do not depend on nationality, sex, ethnic origin, colour, religion, language or any other status.

The Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on 10 December 1948, sets out for the first time the fundamental rights to be universally protected. They include civil and political rights, such as life, liberty and freedom of expression, and economic, social and cultural rights, such as education, health and an adequate standard of living.

Human rights protect human dignity and set limits on how those in power may treat people. They are the foundation of freedom, justice and peace, and they allow every person to take part in the life of their community on an equal footing.

When rights are respected, people can live safely, learn, work, speak freely and seek justice. When they are denied, discrimination, poverty and conflict are more likely to grow.

• Universality – human rights belong to everyone, everywhere.
• Inalienability – rights cannot be taken away, except in specific situations and according to due process.
• Indivisibility and interdependence – civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights are equally important and linked to one another.
• Equality and non-discrimination – every person is entitled to rights without distinction of any kind.
• Participation and inclusion – everyone has the right to take part in decisions that affect them.
• Accountability and the rule of law – those responsible for protecting rights must answer for their actions.

All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. Discrimination means treating people unfairly because of characteristics such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.

Equality before the law and protection against discrimination apply to everyone. States are expected to take active steps to remove barriers that keep people from enjoying their rights.

The Convention on the Rights of the Child (1989) recognises that children have their own rights, including the right to life and development, to education, to health care, to protection from violence, abuse and exploitation, and to be heard in matters that affect them.

In every decision concerning children, their best interests must be a primary consideration.

Women and girls are entitled to the same human rights as everyone else. The Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women (1979) calls for equality in education, work, health, family life and public participation, and for protection from violence and discrimination.

The Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2006) affirms that persons with disabilities have the same rights as everyone else. It stresses dignity, independence, accessibility, reasonable accommodation and full inclusion in society, and the principle that decisions should involve the people they affect.

Everyone has the right to seek asylum from persecution. The 1951 Refugee Convention protects refugees, including through the principle of non-refoulement: people must not be returned to a place where their life or freedom would be at risk.

People displaced within their own country keep all of their rights. The UN Guiding Principles on Internal Displacement describe the protection and assistance they are entitled to receive.

Access to justice means that people can seek and obtain a fair remedy when their rights are violated. It includes equality before the law, the right to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial court, the presumption of innocence, and access to legal information and assistance.

People can only claim their rights if they know them. Human rights education builds knowledge, skills and attitudes that promote respect for rights and equality. It is a continuing process for children, young people and adults, in schools, communities and workplaces, and it is recognised in the UN Declaration on Human Rights Education and Training (2011).

value.text: This handbook defines internal IHRC–USA roles and must be read with the Articles of Association, applicable laws, valid management resolutions and each appointment letter.
value.notice: IMPORTANT: “Ambassador” and “Officer” are internal organisational titles only. They do not confer diplomatic or governmental status, UN or EU recognition, police or investigative powers, judicial authority or a licence to practise law. No appointee may sign contracts, make financial commitments, issue official statements or represent the organisation beyond a specific written delegation.
rules: Every appointment must be in writing and state its term, scope, supervisor, duties and delegated authority.
Salary, honorarium, allowances and expense reimbursement are available only when expressly approved in writing and subject to policy and budget.
No appointee has powers of arrest, search, compulsory questioning, seizure, punishment, legal advice or government direction.
Use the organisation’s name, logo and ID only for authorised work; maintain impartiality, confidentiality, safeguarding and financial integrity.

value.name: Ambassador
value.purpose: Represents IHRC–USA’s mission and approved programmes to communities and institutions within the appointment’s scope.
authority: Introduce the organisation and explain approved programmes in the assigned area.
Coordinate approved awareness events and build community contacts.
Submit activity reports and refer partnership opportunities to management.
duties: Protect the organisation’s reputation and impartiality; communicate accurately; disclose conflicts of interest.
No diplomatic or governmental status is created. Do not sign agreements, fundraise, make commitments or issue official statements without written authority.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Appointment certificate; approved event participation; training and leadership-development opportunities; pre-approved expense reimbursement against receipts, subject to policy.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Goodwill Ambassador
value.purpose: Promotes goodwill, humanitarian values, mutual respect and social harmony.
authority: Promote approved humanitarian and goodwill initiatives.
Participate in approved events and share community feedback.
Respect the dignity and privacy of people receiving assistance.
duties: Remain impartial; obtain informed consent before sharing identifiable stories or images.
Cannot change policy, appoint personnel, promise funding or use the title for private business promotion.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Honorary certificate where approved; relevant training and event participation; contribution letter where verified. No salary is automatic.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Peace Ambassador
value.purpose: Promotes peace, non-violence, conflict prevention, dialogue and reconciliation.
authority: Coordinate approved peace-education and dialogue activities.
Promote tolerance and peaceful communication among youth and communities.
Refer high-risk situations to qualified professionals or lawful authorities.
duties: Prioritise safety, confidentiality and neutrality.
Cannot compel mediation, impose settlements, issue orders or intervene physically in dangerous situations.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Peacebuilding training; approved programme participation; certificates based on verified contribution.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Youth Ambassador
value.purpose: Encourages youth leadership, human-rights education, learning, volunteering and skills development.
authority: Coordinate approved youth events and volunteer groups.
Promote civic awareness, digital safety, education and skills opportunities.
Report youth programme outcomes to management.
duties: Follow child-safeguarding rules, supervision and parental/guardian consent where required.
Do not expose young people to exploitation, unsafe activities or unauthorised publication of personal information.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Leadership(P5) training; approved youth events; participation certificates subject to age and safeguarding rules.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Women Ambassador
value.purpose: Promotes women’s rights, equality, safety, leadership, education and empowerment.
authority: Coordinate approved women’s rights and empowerment activities.
Promote awareness of rights, safety, education and opportunities.
Refer survivors and service needs to qualified organisations.
duties: Respect survivors’ choices, safety, privacy and dignity.
Do not investigate violence, provide clinical treatment or legal advice unless qualified and authorised; never pressure a survivor to reconcile or withdraw a complaint.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Relevant training; approved empowerment programmes; contribution certificates based on verified work.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Ambassador – International Communications
value.purpose: Coordinates approved international correspondence, information exchange, translation support and initial overseas contacts.
authority: Maintain accurate contact records and correspondence.
Translate information faithfully and forward partnership enquiries to management.
Arrange approved meetings and report international opportunities.
duties: Protect personal data and correspondence; respect cultural and language differences.
Do not claim UN, EU, embassy or government endorsement without proof; do not sign MoUs, contracts or funding applications without written authority.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: International communications experience; relevant training; approved event participation; verified contribution letters.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Ambassador At Large
value.purpose: Undertakes special assignments and cross-regional initiatives allocated by IHRC–USA management.
authority: Work only within written terms of reference defining scope, duration and reporting line.
Coordinate approved cross-regional projects and submit progress reports.
Assess regional needs, opportunities and operational risks.
duties: Respect local laws, budgets and delegated authority.
“At Large” does not mean unlimited or worldwide authority; cannot appoint or dismiss officers or change policy without written authority.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Senior project-coordination experience; approved representation opportunities; recognition based on assessed contribution.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Chief Human Rights Investigation Officer
value.purpose: Oversees initial documentation, information assessment and report preparation for human-rights complaints referred to the organisation.
authority: Assess immediate safety risks and refer urgent needs to appropriate services.
Obtain informed consent; record dates, sources and document handling; distinguish verified facts, allegations and unverified information.
Protect records and confidentiality; submit impartial reports with limitations clearly stated.
duties: This is not a police, criminal-investigation, court or government appointment.
No arrest, search, seizure, compulsory questioning, threats, covert surveillance, hacking, unlawful recording or determination of guilt.
Do not enter private premises without lawful permission or alter evidence; do not replace lawyers, doctors or counsellors.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Training in human-rights documentation, safeguarding and reporting; project experience; certificates based on verified work.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Human Rights Officer
value.purpose: Supports human-rights education, community awareness, basic complaint intake, safe documentation and referral.
authority: Conduct approved awareness sessions and provide general rights information.
Listen respectfully, assess immediate safety and record basic information with consent.
Refer people to appropriate legal, medical, psychosocial or public services; prepare anonymised reports.
duties: Respect informed choice, privacy and confidentiality; keep accurate records.
Do not provide legal advice unless qualified, conduct official investigations, declare guilt or promise outcomes.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Human-rights education training; approved programme participation; experience certificates for verified service.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.name: Honorary Member
value.purpose: Recognises a person who supports the organisation through experience, expertise, goodwill or community standing.
authority: Support organisational objectives and attend invited events.
Offer advice, expertise or introductions when invited.
Protect the organisation’s reputation and confidential information.
duties: Honorary status alone does not grant voting rights, directorship, management control or financial authority unless expressly provided by governing documents or resolution.
Do not make commitments or issue official statements on behalf of IHRC–USA.
restrictions: Do not collect financial contributions into a personal account, issue unauthorised receipts, create false credentials, disclose confidential identities, harass or threaten anyone.
benefits: Honorary certificate where approved; invitations to relevant events or advisory discussions; recognition of voluntary contribution.
reporting: Submit periodic reports to the supervisor named in the appointment letter. Performance may be assessed on quality, integrity, timeliness, safeguarding and compliance.

The appointment term is stated in the appointment letter. Following a fair process, appointment may be suspended or ended for misconduct or policy breach. Return organisational property and access credentials when the appointment ends.

value.d: Treat everyone respectfully; discrimination is prohibited.
Reports, certificates and expense claims must be truthful. Fabrication and misleading claims are prohibited.
Use the title, ID card, logo and resources only for authorised work; never imply governmental or diplomatic authority.
Collect only necessary information, store it securely and share it only on a lawful, authorised basis.
Follow child-protection and vulnerable-person safeguarding procedures, including consent and supervision.
Sexual exploitation, harassment, coercion, bullying, intimidation and abuse of authority are prohibited.
Disclose personal, family, political, commercial or financial interests and withdraw from conflicted decisions.
No unauthorised fundraising, personal-account financial contribution collection, false receipts, bribes or commissions.
Do not use IHRC–USA’s name to campaign for a party/candidate or pressure anyone on religion.
Share only approved information; do not publish confidential records, unverified allegations, hate speech or personal data without authority.
Follow applicable laws, permits, safety requirements and organisational policies.
Report misconduct through designated channels; retaliation against good-faith reporters is prohibited.
Threats, violence, humiliation, bullying and unsafe conduct are prohibited.
Protect ID cards, documents, devices and access credentials; return them when the appointment ends.
Promptly report incidents, data breaches and safety risks and cooperate with authorised reviews.

content.value:
The International Human Rights Council – USA (IHRC-USA) has developed a structured framework for granting accreditations and recognitions to individuals, community leaders, non-governmental organizations, and community-based organizations working in the fields of human rights, social justice, education, the protection of women and children, human dignity, and community development.

IHRC-USA firmly believes that accreditation should be more than merely awarding a medal, certificate, or honorary title. It should represent a formal recognition of an individual’s or organization’s service, qualifications, experience, contributions to society, and credibility. All recognitions should be granted through a fair, transparent, and systematic evaluation process based on established criteria and standards.

value:
This form is for applicants seeking a private recognition, programme review or service expressly offered by IHRC-USA. Submission does not guarantee approval.

Unless separately authorized and documented, IHRC-USA recognition is not a government licence, statutory approval, recognized academic accreditation, professional license or authorization to practice a regulated profession.

Complete all applicable fields; write N/A where not applicable; attach copies (not originals) unless specifically requested.

IHRC-USA grants its own institutional accreditations, recognitions and honorary titles in accordance with its organizational policies and established procedures.

Furthermore, ECOSOC Consultative Status with the United Nations is a separate formal status that requires an independent application, review and assessment process by the relevant UN authorities. IHRC-USA’s institutional accreditations do not automatically confer, represent or imply UN ECOSOC Consultative Status.
IHRC-USA is committed to maintaining transparency, credibility, accountability and international standards in all its accreditation and recognition activities.

Members Restrictions & Regulations
lines: 1. No Financial Fundraising: Members are strictly prohibited from collecting or soliciting financial financial contributions under the IHRC-USA name without explicit, written authorization from the SLK Headquarters.
2. No Official Representation: No Members may act, speak, or issue statements to the media as an official international representative of the IHRC-USA without a formal mandate.

3. Non-Compensated Service: All Members positions are strictly unpaid. The IHRC-USA does not provide salaries, and the headquarters is not responsible for personal expenses incurred during Members work.

4. IHRC-USA ID Card Policy: Issued digital or physical Members cards remain the intellectual property of the organization. Misuse, forgery, or public leaks of these documents will lead to immediate termination.
5. Strict Neutrality: In compliance with non-profit standards, Members must remain completely non-partisan. You cannot endorse political parties or candidates using the IHRC-USA affiliation.

6. Content Monitoring: All content posted by Members on the organization’s network is heavily monitored. Individual accounts will be suspended if posts conflict with the core values of the IHRC-USA Headquarters.

intro: Complete all sections. Attach your CV, a one-page research proposal abstract, and copies of certificates. Incomplete applications will not be considered.
Provision of false information will result in cancellation of selection or termination of engagement.

blocks.label: Full Name (in national language, if applicable)

opts: AI & Big Data in Human Rights Monitoring

sections.title: Section H — Preferred Mode of Contribution
Section I — Research Proposal Abstract
sections.note: (Maximum 300 words — attach on a separate sheet)

blocks.label: I hereby declare and undertake that:
items: All information provided in this application is true, complete and accurate.
My research will fully comply with research ethics standards and data protection regulations.
In working with victims, children and vulnerable groups, I will adhere to the “Do No Harm” principle and safeguarding policies.
I will abide by the IHRC-USA Code of Conduct and Confidentiality Undertaking.
I will comply with IHRC-USA policies on the publication rights of research findings.
There is no pending disciplinary action or criminal case against me.
If selected, I agree to submit the required documents and undergo eligibility verification.
